description.value: This study investigated implicit theory-of-mind and intentionality attribution in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia using the Happé-Frith animation task, and examined structural brain correlates of intentionality attribution with voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: We investigate whether bvFTD affects intention attribution tendency while viewing abstract animations and whether this might represent a primary deficit.

value: We investigate whether bvFTD affects intention attribution tendency to abstract animations.
We evaluate whether the propensity to ascribe thoughts and feelings to movement patterns is impaired in bvFTD and whether this is specific to movement patterns displaying mental state manipulation.
Furthermore, we investigate whether any deficits in intentionality attribution can be explained by deficits in cognitive functioning.
We also investigate the regional association of ToM deficits in bvFTD with structural neural integrity. Importantly, we focus on the association that is ToM-specific.

Happé-Frith animation task

description.value: Participants watched animations of two triangles displaying random, goal-directed, or theory-of-mind movement patterns and were instructed to verbally describe what they observed.

spans.text: Subjects are merely instructed to verbally describe what they see, so the instructions contain no reference to mentalizing.
random
These conditions are presumed to respectively trigger animacy perception, agency perception and spontaneous mentalizing.

description.value: Random purposeless movements, with the two triangles bouncing off the walls like billiard balls or merely drifting about; participants described what they observed without explicit reference to mentalizing.

spans.text: goal directed
These conditions are presumed to respectively trigger animacy perception, agency perception and spontaneous mentalizing.

description.value: Goal-directed movements in which one triangle responded to the behaviour of the other, including dancing, chasing, imitating, or one triangle leading the other; participants described what they observed without explicit reference to mentalizing.

spans.text: goal directed movements (GD) where one triangle responded to the behavior of the other one (e.g., ‘following’)
ToM
These conditions are presumed to respectively trigger animacy perception, agency perception and spontaneous mentalizing.

description.value: Theory-of-mind movements in which one triangle anticipated or manipulated the mental state or behaviour of the other, including persuading, bluffing, mocking, or surprising; participants described what they observed without explicit reference to mentalizing.

spans.text: ToM movements, in which one triangle manipulated the other one's mental state or behavior (e.g., ‘seducing’).
